answer:
In `runSearch`, zgrep forces `opts.sort = true` in four cases when `--sort` wasn't passed:

- **`--exec`** (`opts.exec_cmd != null`): it needs to know which files matched, which only the ordered path keeps (src/main.zig:2186-2190).
- **`--heading`**: the streaming path would interleave per-file groups, so headers could point at the wrong cluster (src/main.zig:2191-2195).
- **`--pre`** (`opts.pre_cmd != null`): it runs per file and needs the ordered path (src/main.zig:2196-2197).
- **Several explicit file operands, all regular files**: they are answered in argument order (src/main.zig:2357-2362).

Aliases: `--deterministic` is equivalent to `--sort` (src/main.zig:968-969). Conversely, `-k`/`--kamikaze` sets `sort = false` (src/main.zig:944-946, 1606-1608).

Not shown: whether other code paths (e.g. `--queries-file` batch) set it. The batch runner passes `--sort` explicitly (src/main.zig:1925).
